title: Russian drones are stalking Ukrainian trains and trying to hobble the country's rail system
description: In recent weeks, Russia has stepped up drone strikes on Ukraine's rail network, targeting trains and the approximately 20,000 kilometres of track that form a key transportation artery across the country.
text:
In recent weeks, Russia has stepped up drone strikes on Ukraine's rail network, targeting trains and the approximately 20,000 kilometres of track that form a key transportation artery across the country. When railworkers aboard a train travelling between the Ukrainian cities of Odesa and Dnipro began shouting at passengers to evacuate the carriages early Thursday, Anastasia Rybalchenko's mind immediately began racing through worst-case scenarios. It was 4 a.m., an air-raid alert was in effect, and Russian drones had already struck a number of Ukrainian trains that week, including one just a few kilometres from the Polish border.

Rybalchenko, 17, and other sleepy passengers exited the train and trudged through the grass in a rural area that was about a 15-minute ride from her final destination, Kropyvnytskyi. I didn't understand what was happening or what to do." She quickly learned that it wasn't her train that was on fire, but infrastructure along the railway line. Inside one of Russia’s key targets in its war on Ukraine In recent weeks, Russia has stepped up strikes on Ukraine's rail network, targeting trains and the approximately 20,000 kilometres of track that form a key transportation artery across the country.

With Ukrainian airspace closed, the rail network carries passengers across the country, and in some cases, across the border into Poland.

ด้วยพื้นที่อากาศของอูเครนปิด, เครือข่ายรถไฟจะพาผู้โดยสารข้ามประเทศ, และในบางกรณี,ข้ามชายแดนไปยังโปแลนด์.
